text: What did you pay?
speaker: Enhedu

text: The man's gaze settled on Balag.
speaker: Narrator

text: The first threshold accepted your offering,
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: he said. Then, to Zik:
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: First took a knife I inherited. Ordinary steel. Second took a scar I earned above. Third asked for the name of the woman who waited for me. She used to—
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: He stopped. His mouth worked around a word that would not come.
speaker: Narrator

text: I can still see her face,
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: he said at last.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I just can't remember what anyone ever called her.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Silence settled over the alcove.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun spoke carefully.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: And the fourth?
speaker: Ninsun

text: The man looked at Zik's wrapped hand, at the journal, at the mark that still pulsed faintly beneath the linen.
speaker: Narrator

text: The fourth is why I'm still sitting here. I refused. The City does not force the later payments. It waits. And while it waits, the streets rearrange. The people you arrived with begin to forget why they came. Eventually you forget too—or you decide that whatever is left of you is still too expensive to keep.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: He leaned his head back against the stone.
speaker: Narrator

text: You're marked,
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: he said to Zik.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: That means an account is already open. Everything after this is collection.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: The journal pressed once against Zik's ribs—deliberate, almost like confirmation.
speaker: Narrator

text: The man closed his eyes.
speaker: Narrator

text: Don't give it your name. And if you reach the place where the walls begin to breathe in time with your pulse, turn around. That threshold does not ask. It only records the answer you already gave by arriving.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Balag lowered the axe and offered his hand.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Come with us.
speaker: Balag

text: The man stared at the open hand for a long time.
speaker: Narrator

text: I have followed strangers out of this alcove before,
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: he said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: They always bring me back.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: He did not take the hand.
speaker: Narrator

text: They left him there.
speaker: Narrator

text: As they moved back into the main street, Ninsun spoke almost to herself.
speaker: Narrator

text: The tablets never mentioned survivors.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Behind them, in the narrow alcove, the man began to hum—soft, tuneless, keeping time with a clock only he could still hear.
speaker: Narrator
